feature: International astronaut delegations and national versus joint mission rewards
scope: Seventeen operator-controlled crewed mission programmes. Selection is by country and seat, not named individual astronauts. The purchased Interkosmos research-cosmonaut mission retains its existing contracted-carrier model.

rules.commander: Always national. All unassigned seats remain national; original spacecraft capacities are unchanged.
rules.guests: At most two distinct guest countries, one astronaut per country. A two-seat spacecraft has one guest place. One foreign assignment per guest country at a time; hosting national missions remains possible.
rules.eligibility: Human countries only, not at war with the host. Programme development must already be authorised and its earliest date reached. Cooperation is not restricted to COMECON or to a faction; both governments must consent.
rules.consent: An invitation has a 90-day response deadline. One unresolved invitation popup per guest prevents an old offer from consenting to a replacement. Exact operator, programme, seat and offer serial are checked. Either side can withdraw before departure. Programme cancellation releases guest assignments.
rules.training: First assignment: 26 funded weeks, $0.002bn per week, paid by the guest. No treasury funds means no training progress. A surviving qualified delegation retains its basic course and needs six paid refresher weeks for another assignment; fatal crew loss removes this qualification. Completed training is retained after preflight withdrawal. Partially completed expenditure remains committed.
rules.flight_contribution: Each guest pays 15% of the original mission appropriation, rounded down to whole millions to match native fixed-point money handling. Collected exactly once at guarded departure. The host pays the balance and all original development and operating costs. Every guest must have its contribution available before launch.
rules.reward_share: Each guest receives 20% of the original available reward pool; host share is 100%, 80% or 60%. Applies to programme prestige, scientific data, political power, qualifying general research awards, capped repeat prestige, partial-result prestige and world-first awards. No additional full reward pool is created.
rules.research: A qualifying 10% general award becomes 8%/2% or 6%/2%/2%; a 20% world-first award becomes 16%/4% or 12%/4%/4%. Each country has one use across all technology selectors. Programmes below the original scientific threshold still grant no programme research voucher. Existing world-first and programme receipts remain authoritative; guests receive each programme's participation award once. Previously claimed shares are not redistributed or minted again.
rules.repeat_missions: No repeat science, political power or technology awards. Repeat prestige remains within the original operator programme's total ceiling. A new participant cannot turn an already-claimed operator programme into a fresh full award.
rules.hardware_and_qualification: The operator retains all existing technology, successful-precursor, funding, safety-review and launch-window requirements. A guest gets a joint-flight history record, not independent launcher, spacecraft, lunar-landing capability, domestic programme completion or a free satellite.
rules.flight_roster: Frozen at departure. View navigation and news replay do not alter costs, training, RNG or receipts. Immutable world-first crew records identify the original partners even after later missions.
rules.casualties: National manpower, political losses and personnel fatalities follow actual crew nationality. The operator separately records whole-mission fatalities. For uncrewed assembly launches, assigned astronauts die only after the crewed phase begins. Guest accident reports state national fatalities explicitly. Industrial prestige losses and investigation bills remain with the operator.
rules.human_control: No AI government can propose, accept or begin a guest mission. If a signed guest is taken over by AI after launch, its reward is held for the returning human player; no active AI reward is granted. Crew casualties still belong to their nationality.
rules.risk: Existing programme probability and incident rules apply. Cooperation grants no automatic success-chance bonus. Paid training is a departure requirement. A joint course can cause a missed planetary transfer window.

historical_precedents.title: Sigmund Jaehn: Interkosmos research-cosmonaut flight
historical_precedents.credit: Deutsches Zentrum fuer Luft- und Raumfahrt; factual institutional biography
historical_precedents.precedent: East German research cosmonaut Sigmund Jaehn flew with Soviet commander Valery Bykovsky in 1978 and conducted scientific experiments aboard Salyut 6.
historical_precedents.design_inference: The carrier and command can remain with the operator while a partner supplies a scientific crew member and receives national recognition and research benefits.
historical_precedents.licence_or_permission: Facts paraphrased; no photograph or article copied. Separate reuse permission for page media is unknown.

historical_precedents.title: ESA: Biografie von Sigmund Jaehn
historical_precedents.credit: European Space Agency; factual institutional biography
historical_precedents.precedent: The Soviet Union offered partner-country cosmonaut flights in July 1976. Jaehn and his backup trained from late 1976, with a further mission-specific course before the August 1978 launch.
historical_precedents.design_inference: Guest participation requires prior national approval and funded joint preparation rather than instant seat swapping.
historical_precedents.licence_or_permission: Facts paraphrased; no photograph or article copied. Separate reuse permission for page media is unknown.

balance_not_history: The 20% reward share, 15% appropriation share, 26-week course, six-week refresher, $2m weekly charge and 90-day response period are campaign balance choices, not asserted historical Interkosmos contract terms or historical budgets. Campaign training time is compressed; this is not a model of an astronaut's full career training.

presentation.guest_entry: National Brief shows the active delegation, paid training and a guarded withdrawal control.
presentation.news: Operator and guest-country names appear in local and world reports. The existing MD event frame and photographic assets are reused without alteration.
presentation.preview_status: Offline composition from generated native GUI/GFX and installed font atlases, not an in-game screenshot.
presentation.new_chrome_credit: Custom code-generated native control textures and layout: project implementation by Codex following the user's request. Separate project redistribution licence unknown.
presentation.modifications: Country-seat controls, textual share and training displays, guest history labels and proportionate award figures. No new photograph, watermark or recolouring. Underlying MD and font rights remain separate.
